newsitem.title: SPAIN: Tabacalera slips, but seen unhurt by U.S. deal.
newsitem.headline: Tabacalera slips, but seen unhurt by U.S. deal.

text.p: Shares in Spanish tobacco group Tabacalera slipped on Monday, bucking the market trend, but despite the profit-taking shares were only just off their all-time highs, dealers said.
Tabacalera, 52 percent state owned, slipped 30 pesetas, or 0.38 percent, to 7,890 pesetas, while the IBEX-35 index rose 26.52 points, or 0.39 percent, to 6,788.37.

"Despite the strong moves that the share has had this year, the balance is very good, with a rise of more than 40 percent which makes it logical that there would be some profit-taking," an analyst at a foreign broker said.
Dealers dismissed concerns that a far-reaching U.S. tobacco deal would affect the group or its upcoming privatisation.
Under a tentative agreement reached in the U.S. last week, the U.S. tobacco industry agreed to pay $368.5 billion over 25 years to help U.S. states recoup tax money spent treating ill smokers.
Suing for damages from tobacco addiction is not permitted in Europe, Tabacalera said.

Analysts' focus was on the group's diversification plans. Last week, Tabacalera announced it would buy 20 percent of duty-free shop operator Aldeasa. The move, seen as boosting its retail presence, was warmly received.
